description: baseline

Exploit input structure plus the loose normwise tolerance, since one timed call shares a single structure. Add a cheap per-call detector (offmass = ||A||_1 - ||diag||_1) routing diagonal/zero/identity batches to exact O(n^2) shortcuts (eigenvalues = sorted diagonal, Q = permutation/identity) — a large win on the n=4096 diagonal shape. For dense rows, run a GEMM-heavy approximate eigensolver whose accuracy is rescued cheaply by ONE FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization of Q (the binding orthogonality gate) plus FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L.

Structure detector (offmass via abs().sum) routes diagonal rows to exact O(n^2) sort+permutation shortcut; dense rows fall back to cuSOLVER eigh. Validates (39/39). Benchmark REGRESSED to 292760us vs 255037 baseline: detector overhead (full abs().sum over batch + .all()/.any() CPU syncs + index machinery) tripled the small-n shapes (shape0 4586->13725, shape1 19410->28549). Large dense shapes ~unchanged (cuSOLVER). Need to make detector near-free, esp avoid syncs on small-n.

Near-free detector (one fused abs-sum reduction + single host sync only for all-diagonal case) + cuSOLVER dense. Validates 39/39. Harness benchmark=55711us. IMPORTANT CONTENTION FINDING: I A/B-measured the PLAIN baseline (torch.linalg.eigh) on my exclusive GPU right now = 54112us, NOT 255037. The manager baseline (255037) was measured under heavy fleet contention (all workers active), inflating it ~4.7x. So this 55711 is NOT a real 4.5x win vs plain eigh; under equal clean conditions the detector is a ~3% REGRESSION vs plain eigh (55711 vs 54112). Local-to-local comparisons across workers are only valid at equal fleet load. Real target to beat = ~54000us clean. Per-shape clean baselines: n32=140us n176=5760 n352=17138 n512b640=171287 n1024b60=105889 n2048=158928.

Per-matrix structure router: classifies each matrix in the batch by off-diagonal fraction, routes diagonal rows to O(n^2) shortcut (index_select/index_copy), dense rows to cuSOLVER. Completes the structure-detection half of the brief. Validates 39/39. Benchmark=55577us == iteration2 (55711) == clean baseline (54112), i.e. BENCHMARK-NEUTRAL. The mixed benchmark shapes (6,7) did NOT speed up (shape6 164036 vs clean-baseline 163516) because the mixed profile rarely emits pure-diagonal members and the routing overhead cancels any savings. CONCLUSION: structure routing helps only non-benchmark shapes (n=4096 diagonal test). The benchmark geomean is fully dominated by dense n=512/n=1024 cuSOLVER cost; a real win requires beating cuSOLVER on dense, i.e. tensor-core algorithm.

GEMM-heavy 1-level spectral divide-and-conquer dense path: GEMM-only median (sign-bisection) + sign(A-sigmaI) via batched NS quintic + QR-extracted invariant-subspace bases U+/U- + cuSOLVER on n/2 halves + ONE FP32 NS orthonormalization + FP32 Rayleigh L. MEASURED: FAILS validation on every dense shape (n=512 test3 eigen-residual scaled=8170 vs gate 200; n=1024 scaled=3820; n=2048 scaled=2120). Root cause: the NS matrix-sign converges too slowly near the median split (eigenvalues near sigma stay ~0 under the sign map), so U+/U- are NOT invariant subspaces and Q^T A Q is far from diagonal; recursion would be needed but compounds cost. Also (microbenched) the component costs make it non-viable even if accurate: full QR=4210ms (7x full eigh 569ms!), 2x half-eigh=307ms (only 1.85x cheaper than full, not 4x), eigvalsh-median=465ms, sign(12it)=90ms. Pure-PyTorch GEMM eigensolver cannot beat cuSOLVER: orthonormalization must avoid QR (uses cuSOLVER, 7x cost) and NS-orth needs ~16 iters to converge; no headroom.

Brief explored exhaustively. BEST WORKING HEAD = c1d43e1a (per-matrix structure router + cuSOLVER dense), validates 39/39, benchmark 55577us. TWO MAJOR FINDINGS the manager must act on: (1) CONTENTION ARTIFACT: I A/B-measured plain torch.linalg.eigh on an exclusive GPU = 54112us, NOT the 255037us baseline. The manager baseline was measured under heavy fleet load (~4.7x inflation). So my 55577us is NOT a real ~4.6x win - under equal clean load my router is benchmark-NEUTRAL (~+3% vs plain eigh from detector overhead). Cross-worker local comparisons are only valid at equal fleet load; the manager should re-measure the baseline AND every candidate back-to-back under identical load before ranking. Real target to beat = ~54000us clean. (2) PURE-PYTORCH GEMM EIGENSOLVER IS NON-VIABLE (built+measured, iteration3=commit 0a2bfc5a, validation_error): 1-level spectral-split (NS matrix-sign + QR subspaces + cuSOLVER halves + FP32 NS finish + Rayleigh L) fails accuracy on all dense shapes (n=512 eigen-residual 8170x over gate) because NS-sign converges too slowly near the median split so the subspaces aren't invariant. Component microbench proves NO headroom even if accurate: full QR=4210ms = 7x full eigh(569ms)!; NS-orthonormalization needs ~16 iters; 2x half-eigh=307ms is only 1.85x cheaper than full (cuSOLVER cost isn't pure n^3). The structure-detection half of the brief is correct but only helps NON-benchmark shapes (the n=4096 diagonal shape is in tests:, not benchmarks:; mixed benchmark shapes rarely contain pure-diagonal members). RECOMMENDATION: the eigh benchmark geomean is fully dominated by SIMT-bound serial cuSOLVER on dense n=512/n=1024 (profile-confirmed: sytrd/symv/gemv/laed, zero tensor-core). Beating it REQUIRES a custom-CUDA tensor-core batched solver (the block-Householder/Jacobi/sign-D&C kernels workers 1/2/4 own) - pure PyTorch (bmm/QR/eigh/solve) cannot, because every orthonormalization primitive except bmm is itself a cuSOLVER call as slow as or slower than eigh. Suggest next brief for me: a custom load_inline kernel (e.g. SMEM-resident batched Jacobi for the small/medium-n shapes n<=176 that DO fit in 228KB SMEM), or fold my structure-router onto whichever worker's dense tensor-core solver wins.

Settle the question the whole search hinges on: can a GEMM-ONLY (torch.bmm in FP16/BF16/TF32, FP32 accumulate) spectral solver beat ~54k us clean on the dominant n=512 b=640 dense shape? Build a LEAN, FIXED-iteration matrix-sign / Newton-Schulz spectral splitter using ONLY bmm + cheap elementwise — strictly NO torch.linalg.eigh/qr/solve/cholesky in the hot path (W3 proved that cuSOLVER glue is itself eigh-slow). Per-matrix norm prescale; a few fixed sign iterations to form projector (I+sign)/2; deflate via bmm; finish with bmm-only FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization + Rayleigh-quotient L. Commit and benchmark each iteration even if slow/inaccurate at first — the committed n=512 timing AND normwise residual are the datapoint. Emit FP32 Q, ascending L.

PROBE iter1: recursive bmm-only spectral D&C (NS-quintic sign 12it -> projector -> NS-orth bases 12it -> project -> recurse to 2x2 closed form; FP32 NS finish + Rayleigh L). N512 b640 DATAPOINT: time=1435ms (8x SLOWER than clean eigh 171ms), eig_resid=0.42, orth_resid=2.90 (both FAIL; gates eig<0.012 orth<3.1 but scaled orth_resid=2.9 raw is way over). Two problems: (1) SLOW: deep recursion makes 1023 Python _dc calls with hundreds of tiny launch-bound bmms at deep levels (n=2,4,8). (2) INACCURATE: NS-orth of projector leading-columns doesn't converge (orth_resid 2.9 means Q far from orthonormal; 2 finish-NS steps cannot rescue an assembled Q that far off). Next: breadth-first single-batched-call-per-level to kill launch overhead, and fix orthonormalization (the projector leading-k columns are rank-deficient/ill-conditioned so NS-orth stalls).

PROBE iter2: breadth-first bmm-only spectral D&C (one batched bmm call per split level over all 2^level blocks stacked into the batch; sign10+orth10 per level, per-level full [I-P|P] NS-orthonormalization, 4 levels, identity leaf). SPEED DATAPOINT n512 b640 = 280ms (vs clean eigh 171ms harness / 569ms microbench): the bmm-only pipeline is ~1.6x SLOWER than harness-clean-eigh and only ~2x faster than microbench-eigh -- and that is WITH a trivial identity leaf (no real leaf solver). ACCURACY: eig_resid=0.43, harness fails every shape (scaled 1000-122000x over gate). DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING (proven separately with EXACT components - exact median via eigvalsh, exact sign via eigh, exact QR bases): a bmm-only spectral D&C, which MUST recurse fully because eigh is banned, has eig_resid that JUMPS from 0.0095 (1 split + eigh-on-256-halves, would pass) to 0.369 at >=2 split levels and PLATEAUS there for 2..7 levels - INDEPENDENT of sign/orth/precision. Root cause: after the first split the sub-block UpT A Up has ~1% invariant-subspace leak; splitting it again at its (now-meaningless) median mixes the already-leaky directions and the error saturates ~0.37. The split structure ONLY clears tolerance with <=1 split followed by eigh on the halves (=W2's approach, which W3 already proved is eigh-slow). CONCLUSION: the fully-bmm-only spectral solver lineage is RETIRED on both axes - cannot clear the 0.0122 eigen gate at any recursion depth, and isn't decisively faster than eigh even ignoring accuracy.

BRIEF 1 SETTLED — DECISIVE NEGATIVE: a fully bmm-only matrix-sign/Newton-Schulz spectral D&C CANNOT beat ~54k at tolerance on n=512, and isn't even decisively faster than eigh. Two built+benchmarked iterations (both validation_error, harness-confirmed): iter0 recursive (1435ms, eig_resid 0.42); iter1 breadth-first one-batched-call/level (280ms, eig_resid 0.43). SPEED: the leanest bmm-only pipeline (4 levels, identity leaf, sign10+orth10) = 280ms = ~1.6x SLOWER than harness-clean-eigh (171ms), only ~2x faster than microbench-eigh (569ms), and that EXCLUDES a real leaf solver. So it does not decisively clear 54k even ignoring accuracy. ACCURACY CEILING (rigorously isolated with EXACT components — exact median via eigvalsh, exact sign via eigh, exact QR bases): eig_resid jumps 0.0095 (1 split + eigh-on-256-halves, passes) -> 0.369 at >=2 split levels and PLATEAUS at 0.369 for 2..7 levels, INDEPENDENT of sign/orth/precision. Mechanism: the first split's sub-block UpT A Up carries ~1% invariant-subspace leak (eigenvalues straddling the median); splitting that leaky block again at its now-meaningless median mixes the wrong directions and saturates ~0.37. Eigenvalues arbitrarily close to the median make the sign map (flat at 0) unable to converge there in finite iterations, so no amount of sign iterations fixes it — confirmed because the exact-sign test ALSO gave 0.37. The split structure only clears tolerance with <=1 split THEN eigh on the n/2 halves — which is exactly W2's Jacobi-on-sub-blocks lane that I already proved is eigh-slow (QR=7x eigh, half-eigh only 1.85x cheaper). RECOMMENDATION: RETIRE the pure-bmm-only spectral/sign lineage (W1's full recursive D&C will hit the same per-level-leak compounding wall; suggest it pivot or be capped at 1 split + a fast sub-solver). The ONLY remaining path to beat clean ~54k on dense n=512/1024 is a custom-CUDA tensor-core kernel that does the per-matrix tridiagonalization/Jacobi in registers+SMEM (W4/W5 lane), NOT PyTorch glue. For my next brief I'd take: a custom load_inline batched kernel for the n<=176 shapes (fit one matrix in 228KB SMEM), or harden+ship my brief-0 structure-router (commit c1d43e1a) onto the winning dense solver.

You proved the pure-torch.bmm-only spectral lineage is dead (leak saturates at 0.37 beyond 1 split; 280ms > 171ms clean-eigh). Pivot to the one tensor-core mechanism no worker owns: a custom load_inline batched ONE-SIDED block-JACOBI for the dominant n=512 b=640 shape — distinct from W1 (sign-fn), W4 (Householder tridiag), W2 (eigh-glue). One matrix (or block-pair) per threadblock; Brent-Luk round-robin pairing; FIXED small sweep count (no convergence test); apply the block rotations as WMMA/mma.sync GEMMs in BF16/TF32 + FP32 accumulate (sm_100a, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0a); per-matrix norm prescale; recover eigenvalue signs via Rayleigh quotient; finish with FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization (binding 100*n*eps gate) and ascending L. One-sided Jacobi avoids the spectral-split leak entirely (it converges off-diagonal mass directly, not via projector recursion). Land a working+committed iteration first, then optimize the rotation GEMM. Keep Xsyevbatched for n>=1024 via a per-shape router if helpful.

MILESTONE: custom load_inline batched ONE-SIDED block-JACOBI kernel WORKS. Design: shift A->A+cI (c=max abs row sum) to make PD (removes +/-lambda one-sided-Jacobi degeneracy -- validated: indefinite plain one-sided Jacobi floored at eig 0.015, shift-PD reaches 0.0002); block-cols BW=16, one (matrix,block-pair) per threadblock per Brent-Luk round (host loops 31 rounds x 8 sweeps = 248 kernel launches); per block: load 512x32 panel to SMEM, Gram=B^T B, inner 32x32 two-sided Jacobi with PARALLEL (Brent-Luk) rotations, apply 32x32 rotation to B and V panels, write back; Rayleigh L=diag(V^T A V), ascending. CORRECTNESS: passes 37/39 incl all dense n=512 (eig 0.0053, orth 1.6e-3); FAILS only test11 (n=512 repeated-eigenvalue, eig 0.31 vs 0.22) and test19 (n=512 mixed) -- degenerate spectra need >8 sweeps. SPEED (scratch, n=512): ~120ms/matrix, b=640 extrapolates to ~76s -- far too slow for harness benchmark. Bottleneck: 136KB SMEM/block -> only 1 block/SM (148 concurrent vs 10240 needed -> 70 waves), and FP32 SMEM-loop GEMMs (no tensor cores yet). Next: WMMA/tensor-core GEMMs for Gram+apply, shrink SMEM (FP16 panels) to raise occupancy, +2 sweeps for degenerate robustness.

OPTIMIZE iter2: BW=8 (was 16). Smaller blocks => MORE ACCURATE (dense n=512 eig 0.00084 vs 0.0053 at BW=16, well under gate) and cheaper inner solve. SPEED b=640 extrapolated ~12s (was 76s; 6x faster) at sweeps=10 inner=3. KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING via inner_sweeps sweep: the inner 2Wx2W Jacobi is ~70% of cost, but the FLOOR with a FREE inner solve (inner=0) is still 4.4s for b=640 -- dominated by 630 kernel relaunches/solve (63 Brent-Luk rounds x 10 sweeps) + low occupancy (panel SMEM => ~1-3 blocks/SM => many waves) + per-round Gram recompute+panel IO. So the per-round-RELAUNCH design cannot beat eigh (171ms) regardless of inner-solve speed. VIABILITY VERDICT (partial): the Jacobi DIRECTION is viable in principle -- the GEMM-only FLOP floor for 8 sweeps b640 is ~2-20ms with tensor cores (vs eigh 171ms) -- but requires (a) fusing all rounds into ONE kernel (no relaunch, keep V/state resident across rounds), (b) tensor-core WMMA for Gram+apply, (c) high occupancy. Next iter3: single-kernel-per-matrix rewrite that loops all rounds internally.

OPTIMIZE iter3: FUSED single-kernel-per-matrix (one block owns one matrix, loops whole Brent-Luk schedule internally -> ZERO per-round relaunches, V stays resident). Correct (dense n=512 eig 0.0011, orth 1.6e-3). SPEED b=640 = 15.7s -- SLOWER than iter2 relaunch (12s)! Finding: removing relaunch overhead did NOT help; the bottleneck is the TOTAL WORK done as many tiny synced SMEM ops. At BW=8, nblk=64 => 32 pairs/round x 63 rounds x 10 sweeps = ~20,160 panel-ops/matrix, each Gram(512x16x16)+inner-16x16-Jacobi+apply(512x16x16); with only 640 blocks (~3/SM) the long serial per-block chain dominates and parallelism dropped vs relaunch's 10240 blocks. VIABILITY ASSESSMENT: the one-sided block-Jacobi DIRECTION is sound (correct, no spectral-leak ceiling, shift-PD validated) and the GEMM-only FLOP floor is ~2-20ms with tensor cores, but BEATING eigh requires (1) WMMA/mma tensor-core Gram+apply GEMMs (currently FP32 SMEM loops), (2) a much cheaper inner 2Wx2W solve (it is 70-95% of cost), (3) larger BW to cut panel-op count. My 3 working impls land at 12-76s (70-450x eigh); the remaining gap is a multi-day tensor-core kernel optimization, not an algorithmic blocker.

CORRECTION/MILESTONE: ran the FULL harness benchmark on iter3 (fused one-sided block-Jacobi, BW=8, sweeps=10 inner=3) -- it COMPLETED and PASSED correctness on ALL 13 benchmark shapes, emitting a real geomean = 191816 us. (My prior row for this commit guessed N/A/timeout; this is the actual verdict.) Per-shape: the 5 n=512 shapes (3,6,8,9,11) each ~4.47s (my Jacobi kernel, 26x slower than cuSOLVER's 0.17s), other 8 shapes use cuSOLVER eigh fallback. So it is a correct-but-slow REGRESSION vs ~54k clean baseline. This is the WORKING+COMMITTED milestone the brief asked for: a custom load_inline batched one-sided block-Jacobi that produces leaderboard-valid eigendecompositions on the dominant n=512 shape. Bottleneck remains the FP32 SMEM-loop inner-solve+GEMMs (not tensor-cored); the GEMM-only FLOP floor is ~2-20ms with tensor cores so the direction can win with a WMMA rewrite + cheaper inner solve.

BRIEF 2 DONE. DELIVERED: a WORKING+COMMITTED+HARNESS-BENCHMARKED custom load_inline batched one-sided block-Jacobi for n=512 (HEAD=9b3a54f1, BW=8 fused). It PASSES correctness on all 13 benchmark shapes and emits a real geomean = 191816 us. VIABILITY VERDICT for the Jacobi tensor-core direction: ALGORITHMICALLY SOUND but NOT YET FAST. (1) WORKS - unlike the spectral-split lineage I killed, one-sided Jacobi has NO leak ceiling; it converges off-diagonal mass directly. The KEY enabler I found+validated: SHIFT A->A+cI (c=max abs row sum) to make it positive-definite -- plain one-sided Jacobi on indefinite symmetric A floors at eig_resid 0.015 because it implicitly diagonalizes A^2 and can't separate lambda from -lambda; shift-PD reaches eig 0.0008 in 8-10 sweeps. (2) NOT FAST - my 3 impls (per-round-relaunch BW16/BW8, fused-single-kernel BW8) land at 12-76s for b=640 = 70-450x cuSOLVER (0.17s); the n=512 shapes alone are ~4.47s each. Bottleneck precisely isolated (via inner_sweeps=0..3 sweep): the FP32 SMEM-loop inner 2Wx2W Jacobi is 70-95% of cost; even with a FREE inner solve the relaunch floor is 4.4s (630 launches + low occupancy from 136KB-panel SMEM=>1-3 blocks/SM); BW=8 beats BW=16 (bigger inner solve dominates); FUSING all rounds into one kernel did NOT help (15.7s) because the work is op-bound not launch-bound. (3) PATH TO WIN is clear but is a multi-day kernel effort: the GEMM-only FLOP floor for 8 sweeps b640 is ~2-20ms with tensor cores, so WMMA/mma BF16 Gram+apply GEMMs + a cheap/cheaper inner solve (the non-GEMM 70-95%) + raised occupancy CAN beat eigh. RECOMMENDATION: the direction is worth pouring a tensor-core kernel specialist at (distinct from W1 sign-fn / W4 Householder), but it is NOT a quick win; if the fleet needs a near-term n=512 win, W4's WMMA Householder-tridiag or W1's tensor-core-ized sign solver are likely closer. My committed kernel is a correct, leaderboard-valid starting point for the WMMA optimization. For my next brief: either (a) tensor-core-ize THIS kernel's Gram+apply (continue), or (b) pivot to hardening the structure-router (brief-0 c1d43e1a) onto whichever dense solver wins.

Continue your working custom one-sided block-Jacobi (9b3a54f1, passes all 13 shapes) and attack its dominant cost center FIRST in isolation: route the Gram (A^T A block) and apply (rotation) GEMMs — the 70-95% of runtime you profiled — onto Blackwell tensor cores via WMMA/mma.sync in BF16/TF32 with FP32 accumulate (sm_100a, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0a), keeping the shift-to-PD trick and FP32 Newton-Schulz finish. Land that single change committed+benchmarked as a clean go/no-go: your FLOP floor says 2-20ms is reachable, so the kernel-time delta from tensor-core GEMMs alone tells you if the thesis holds before touching the coupled inner-2Wx2W-solve / SMEM-occupancy levers. If it moves the needle, then go after the inner solve + smaller panel for occupancy next. Benchmark clean idle min-of-3 (real bar: remote cuSOLVER 49,740us, #1 33,954us). Emit FP32 Q ascending.

SINGLE-LEVER GO/NO-GO: tensor-core the Gram (B^T B) GEMM of the one-sided block-Jacobi. RESULT = NO net win (decisive signal to stop the multi-day part). Clean back-to-back harness A/B under identical conditions: FP32-SIMT-Gram (iter3) = 191703us; 3xTF32-WMMA-Gram (this commit, passes all 13 shapes) = 217967us -> tensor cores are SLOWER (n=512 solve 4.47s -> 6.23s). ROOT CAUSE: block-Jacobi's per-block-pair GEMMs are tiny 16x16 outputs (PW=16); WMMA's warp-granular fixed 16x16x8 tiles have no throughput edge there, while the FP32-SIMT Gram uses all 256 threads fully. Confirmed fair: tried warp-0-only (1941ms inner=0) AND all-8-warp K-split (2130ms inner=0) tensor-core Gram; both lose to FP32-SIMT (the brief's 2-20ms FLOP-floor assumes LARGE GEMMs, which this kernel does not have). PRECISION SUB-FINDINGS (reusable): BF16 Gram fails (eig 0.08), BF16 W-apply catastrophic (eig 0.78); plain TF32 Gram marginal (clustered needs 24 sweeps vs 10); TF32/BF16 W-apply FATAL (rounds the small off-diagonals being zeroed); 3xTF32 error-corrected Gram (x=hi+lo split, 3 mma) RECOVERS ~FP32 accuracy at 10 sweeps incl clustered; V-accumulator apply MUST stay FP32 (BF16 destroys orthonormality over ~20k rotations). The shift-to-PD trick creates a high-dynamic-range Gram that is hostile to low precision. CONCLUSION: tensor cores are the wrong lever for THIS kernel; the inner 2Wx2W solve (62% of cost) and occupancy are where the time is, but they are not GEMMs. To make tensor cores pay you would need a fundamentally different blocking (large panels), which reintroduces the inner-solve explosion I measured in brief 2.

BRIEF 3 SETTLED. SINGLE-LEVER GO/NO-GO (tensor-core the Gram + apply GEMMs) = decisive NO. Clean back-to-back harness A/B under identical fleet conditions: FP32-SIMT-Gram = 191703us; 3xTF32-WMMA-Gram (committed 94e25ddc, passes all 13 shapes) = 217967us. Tensor cores are SLOWER (n=512 solve 4.47s->6.23s). ROOT CAUSE (the decisive insight): block-Jacobi's per-block-pair GEMMs are TINY 16x16 outputs (PW=16), and WMMA's warp-granular fixed 16x16x8 tiles have zero throughput advantage at that size, whereas the FP32-SIMT Gram saturates all 256 threads. The brief's 2-20ms FLOP floor assumed LARGE GEMMs; this kernel doesn't have them. Verified fair (not a strawman): tested warp-0-only AND all-8-warp-K-split tensor-core Gram -- both lose to FP32-SIMT. The W-apply can't even be lowered: TF32/BF16 there is FATAL (rounds the small off-diagonals being zeroed), and the V accumulator must stay FP32 (BF16 destroys orthonormality over ~20k rotations). REUSABLE SUB-FINDING: 3xTF32 error-correction (operand = hi+lo TF32 split, 3 mma passes, drop lo*lo) recovers ~FP32 Gram accuracy at 10 sweeps including the clustered shape that plain TF32 needs 24 sweeps for -- but it's still net-slower here. The shift-to-PD trick (needed for +/-lambda) makes the Gram high-dynamic-range, hostile to low precision. VERDICT: the multi-day tensor-core kernel push is NOT warranted for this one-sided-Jacobi design -- the 62%-of-cost inner 2Wx2W solve and the occupancy ceiling are the real bottlenecks and they are NOT GEMMs. To make tensor cores pay you'd need fundamentally larger panels, which reintroduces the inner-solve explosion measured in brief 2 (BW=16 fused timed out >10min). RECOMMENDATION: retire the tensor-core-the-Jacobi-GEMMs line. The fleet's near-term n=512 win is more likely W4's WMMA Householder-tridiag (whose back-transform IS a large GEMM) or W1's tensor-core sign solver. For my next brief: I'd pivot to hardening my brief-0 structure-router (c1d43e1a, validated, benchmark-neutral) onto whichever dense solver wins, OR profile the inner-solve to see if a register-resident 2x2-batched inner Jacobi (no SMEM syncs) could cut the 62%.

Your go/no-go was decisive: one-sided Jacobi is structurally ceilinged (16x16 block-pair GEMMs too tiny for tensor cores), so retire it. Redeploy your tensor-core + 3xTF32 expertise onto the LARGE-GEMM dense play that W1 is building. Build, as standalone reusable components for the direct two-stage solver, the two large-GEMM pieces where tensor cores DO pay: (1) the eigenvector BACK-TRANSFORM Q = H_1...H_p S applied as one big batched bmm over the full (B,n,n) batch at n=512/1024, and (2) your proven 3xTF32 error-correction GEMM (operand = hi+lo TF32 split, 3 mma passes, drop lo*lo) as a drop-in 'FP32-grade matmul on tensor cores' so these large GEMMs hold the tight orthogonality/eigen gates that plain TF32/BF16 fails. Validate the components in a minimal end-to-end pipeline (your shift-to-PD and Newton-Schulz finish transfer). The goal is a clean, profiled back-transform + FP32-grade-TC-GEMM that W1's two-stage solver adopts via combine. set_float32_matmul_precision where it helps; emit FP32 Q ascending; benchmark clean idle min-of-3.

DELIVERED 2 reusable large-GEMM components for the two-stage dense solver (composable via combine), validated end-to-end (passes ALL 39 test shapes; harness geomean 124742us -- the n=512 path runs the back-transform pipeline live). COMPONENT 1 fp32_grade_bmm(A,B): cuBLASLt CUDA-13 BF16x9 FP32 emulation (CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9, EAGER strategy, +256MB workspace +heuristic algo select -- workspace+algo were the unlock, naive call was no faster). CLEAN MIN-OF-3: n512 b640 BF16x9=1.45ms(relerr 3.2e-7) vs FP32 2.91ms vs TF32 0.33ms => 2.01x faster than FP32 at FP32-GRADE accuracy; n1024 2.32x; n2048 2.59x. COMPONENT 2 back_transform(U,S)=U@S via component1. KEY VALIDATION (the precision-enabler thesis CONFIRMED): a TF32 back-transform Q=U@S FAILS the orthogonality gate at n=512 (||Q^T Q-I||~0.0085 > 0.0061 allowed, scaled 138) because TF32's 3e-4 GEMM error accumulates over the n=512 row reductions; BF16x9 HOLDS it (relerr 3e-7 -> orth scaled 0.78, passes w/ margin). So plain TF32/BF16 is unusable for the back-transform but BF16x9 gives FP32-grade at 2x+ tensor-core speed. NOTE: cuBLASLt must run on the default queue (handle 0) -- the leaderboard bans the 'stream' token (substring-matched), so no getCurrentCUDAStream; +cudaDeviceSynchronize for safety. W1 combines: replace my random-orthogonal reduction stand-in with the real Householder reduction U; the back-transform + fp32_grade_bmm drop straight in.
